component.name: FujiNet Go CoCo
component.summary: Self-contained Tandy Color Computer with built-in FujiNet

description.p: A Tandy Color Computer with FujiNet built in: mount disk images from TNFS servers or the local SD folder, configure everything through the embedded FujiNet web UI, and play with automatic gamepad support driving the analog joystick ports.

Emulation is provided by XRoar, with FujiNet attached over the Becker port -- DriveWire carried on loopback TCP -- so HDB-DOS finds it as its boot device and the machine drops straight into FujiNet's CONFIG. Both the Color Computer 2 and the Color Computer 3 are supported, and you can switch between them without restarting.

screenshot.caption: FujiNet CONFIG running on the emulated Color Computer 3

description.p: The bundled FujiNet runtime moves back onto upstream master. The previous build came from force-mbedtls-3, a branch that was never merged, so the runtime had been standing still while upstream moved on. The Mbed TLS 3.x requirement it was branched for has landed, and the device-chain rework and the Drivewire cassette media format arrive with it.

The bundled FujiNet runtime moves to a firmware build that refuses to compile against Mbed TLS 4.x. That release removed the low-level crypto headers the runtime's TLS backend needs and split the rest into a separate library, so a machine whose system Mbed TLS had moved to 4.x could produce a build with broken TLS instead of a clear failure. The build now finds a 3.x install, or stops and says so.
It also picks up Gmail message composition, and the calendar protocols gain the ability to create and edit events rather than only read them.

The bundled FujiNet runtime moves up to a firmware build with the new calendar network protocols. A program running on the emulated CoCo can open CALENDAR:, GCAL: and ICAL: URLs on the N: device and read a Google Calendar or iCalendar feed straight off the network device.

The debugger's C source stepping now handles programs built from several .c files: select every module's .lst at once (or load them one at a time), and each adds its own functions, lines and locals rather than replacing what was already loaded. CMOC names the linker map after the final executable, not any one source file, so a multi-module build's shared .map is now found even when it doesn't share a listing's name.

The debugger now steps through C source, for programs built with CMOC. Load a listing (from `cmoc -i`) and get a source pane with the current line marked, breakpoints set by clicking a line, Step Line/Step Over Line alongside the existing instruction-level stepping, and a Locals pane showing parameters and locals by name and value.

Fixed the debugger's video pane rendering a corrupted picture on the Color Computer 3. Its GIME scanline counter never restarted at each character row, so the pane read screen memory several times too fast and drew glyph rows that do not exist; Color Computer 2 machines were unaffected.

The same pane now also honours the GIME's horizontal offset and 256-byte virtual-screen registers, and reproduces the hardware quirk that blanks half the data in 16-colour, 16-byte-per-row graphics modes.
Windows now ships an NSIS installer alongside the portable zip, and macOS gets a proper packaged release, matching the sibling ADAM and Apple II desktop apps' own release process.
Native Windows and macOS builds join Linux: both are full Win32/ AppKit frontends, not ports of a shared toolkit, with their own debugger windows and Settings dialogs.

The debugger gained a decoded video pane, HD6309 disassembly alongside the 6809, and symbol loading (LWASM's --symbol-dump format, plus a small built-in table of Color BASIC ROM entry points). The Color Computer's CPU (6809/HD6309) can now be switched live, the same way the machine and TV input already could. CI now covers Linux, macOS, Windows and flatpak on every push, and released packages include .deb/.rpm/.tar.gz alongside the flatpaks.
First release of the Color Computer desktop app: a headless XRoar core driven on a vsync-phase-locked emulator thread, with the FujiNet firmware built in-process and joined over the Becker port.
